correctness.rationale: The source paper's exact length-two character criterion turns a successful direct torus probe into a quadratic-character indicator. Exact fiber counting for beta -> N(S-beta) converts the success count to a squarefree quartic character sum, whose smooth projective genus-one model has exactly twice as many rational points as successful probes. Hasse's bound yields the uniform half-density estimate. Uniqueness of the residual two-term decomposition and the source paper's no-equal-or-opposite property give the exact factor-three conversion to minimum-weight coset leaders. Exhaustive finite checks for q=9,27,81 reproduce both identities and the bounds.

originality.rationale: The closest recent paper gives the direct torus search only a worst-case q+1 probe bound and gives its separate structured parameter searches asymptotic density 1/4; it does not state the direct-search half-density, the elliptic-curve point-count identity, or the weight-three coset-leader multiplicity formula. Targeted searches found no equivalent statement. Older Zetterberg decoding sources were only partly accessible, so residual folklore, older-literature, and near-simultaneous priority risk remains material.

value.rationale: The theorem changes the quantitative understanding of the recent direct decoder from a possible full scan of q+1 torus elements to 2+O(q^{-1/2}) expected probes uniformly over every hard syndrome, identifies the exact elliptic-curve mechanism behind this density, and simultaneously quantifies the number of maximum-likelihood weight-three error patterns in every hard coset.
